Emma H: quick sync — int4 bringup for codegen-2 saw a tiny quality dip on our unit tests, want to decide gating thresholds before we push to 5% canary
Kai P: saw that morning too, can you paste the smoke numbers?
Emma H: model-ci-bot posted the run, but quick summary: pass@1 down 0.8% absolute on codegen-small suite, perplexity +2.2%. latency median +6ms, p95 +18ms
model-ci-bot: CI summary: branch=int4-onboard, dataset=codegen-small, samples=3k, pass@1: baseline=34.1% -> candidate=33.3% (-0.8), ppl: 12.4 -> 12.66 (+2.2%), tail-latency p95: 220ms -> 238ms (+8.2%)
Ryan M: thanks. Is the pass@1 drop concentrated on certain prompt types?
Emma H: yeah, mainly multi-line code prompts and long-context docstrings. single-line completions fine. Repro shows higher hallucination rate for prompts > 512 tokens
Simon D: can we break down by quantization path? nf4 vs int4-perf vs int4-stable?
Emma H: nf4-int4 (our default) shows the largest delta. int4-stable has smaller perf gains but almost no quality delta. nf4-int4 has ~1.1% pass@1 drop on the long prompts slice
Kai P: okay. Proposal for rollout gates: 1) start at 0.5% traffic 2) hold 60m, require delta(pass@1) >= -0.3% absolute AND ppl change <= +1.0% AND p95 latency <= +10% 3) if pass, move to 5% hold 2h with same checks 4) 20% hold 6h 5) full if green. If any check fails, auto-fallback to previous model
Ryan M: +1 to thresholds but want an absolute fallback threshold for alerts: if pass@1 drop > 0.5% at any stage -> auto-rollback. Also if 5xx rate increases by >0.2% absolute -> rollback
Simon D: add sample-based guard: run 500 shadow eval calls with our regression test prompts; if %inputs with syntactic errors increases > 0.4% -> fail
Emma H: added. Also suggest canary sampling strategy: stratified sampling by prompt-length buckets (<=128, 129-512, >512) to ensure long-context coverage at early stages
Kai P: good. For automation, I can add a gating config in rollout YAML:```yaml
canary:
  steps:
    - pct: 0.5
      hold: 60m
    - pct: 5
      hold: 120m
    - pct: 20
      hold: 360m
checks:
  pass_at_1_abs_delta: -0.3
  ppl_rel_max: 1.0 # percent
  p95_latency_rel_max: 10.0 # percent
  five_xx_abs_spike: 0.2 # percent
  shadow_sample_count: 500
  shadow_error_delta_pct: 0.4
fallback: auto
notifications:
  - channel: #eng-ml
  - on_fail: paging
```
Ryan M: ping @Kai P when you add it. Also set a quick smoke-run after the 0.5% step that runs a single A/B slice comparing 2k real requests in quiet-burn for 30m
Emma H: FYI we also want to flag any semantic regressions: if eval-based BLEU-like score on the docstring suite drops >0.6 absolute -> block
Simon D: agree. Last ask: add hysteresis so we don't flipflop on minor noise. require two consecutive green checks at same stage to promote when pct>=5
Kai P: will implement hysteresis + the stratified sampling. I'll add the rollout with `redwood rollout create --from=hf:codegen-2-int4 --to=hf:codegen-2-int8 --config=canary.yaml` and set automatic fallback.
model-ci-bot: scheduled shadow-eval job: job_id=shadow-231234-1, expected duration 35m, will post metrics to /metrics/rollouts/2312345678
Emma H: thanks. After 0.5% hold I want a quick postmortem template if we see regression (who, what, mitigations, rollback steps, follow-ups)
Ryan M: I'll draft the template, keep it short. Emma, Simon — you two own analysis if we need to dig in. Kai owns the rollout automation
Kai P: will notify here when rollout created and when 0.5% job finishes
Emma H: cool. If anything goes red during the 0.5% hold, we keep it blocked and run int4-stable variant as fallback for long-context. :thumbsup:
Simon D: good plan.
Kai P: starting work now, ETA ~2h for config and shadow job kick-off
Emma H: thanks everyone.
